Flutter example build files distributed XCSSET malware

Target: universal_file_viewer · repo
Date: 2026-09-08
Target Kind: application
Language: Shell
Impact: credential_theft
Phase: source

Synopsis

The universal_file_viewer 0.1.5 archive on pub.dev contained infected example build files from a compromised maintainer workstation. Building the example could execute XCSSET; ordinary dependency use did not compile those files.

Story

A Flutter package's demonstration app carried malware even though the library developers ordinarily imported was clean. On September 8, Aikido researcher Ilyas Makari reported XCSSET in universal_file_viewer 0.1.5 on pub.dev. The package provided document and media preview widgets; the dangerous files accompanied it in the example project that showed developers how to use them.

Aikido attributed the contamination to a maintainer's infected workstation, where the worm modified local build files before publication. The retained pub.dev archive confirmed the distinction: the affected paths were under example/, including Android's Gradle configuration and the iOS and macOS Xcode projects. Adding the library as a dependency did not build that demonstration. A developer explicitly building the example entered a different execution path from an application merely using the preview widgets.

The Android configuration attached a hidden shell command to a preBuild task. The Xcode projects embedded build rules and encoded commands that contacted remote infrastructure. Those were instructions for the developer's build tools, rather than Dart features needed to display a document. Aikido's broader payload analysis described XCSSET modules for stealing browser and other local data and modifying additional projects, explaining how one workstation infection could become another maintainer's published source.

The pub.dev version record marks 0.1.5 as retracted, and the captured archive's digest matches the registry's published value. That establishes what the registry distributed without turning every package download into a confirmed infection. The cited investigation did not identify how many developers built the infected example. Its narrow execution condition mattered: the package was compromised upstream, but ordinary dependency use and local example development did not carry the same exposure.
